acceptance_criteria.criterion: GET /api/projects returns 200 with a JSON array of all projects
POST /api/projects returns 201 on valid input and 400 on missing required fields
PUT /api/projects/:id/rename returns 200 with the renamed project, or 404 if not found
POST /api/projects/:id/repositories returns 200 when the repo is successfully linked, or 404 if project or repo does not exist
DELETE /api/projects/:id/repositories/:repoId returns 204 on success, or 404 if the association does not exist
All 8 route handlers are covered by unit tests using mock manager instances

comments.note: PUT /api/projects/:id/rename distinguishes 404 vs 400 by checking whether the manager error message contains 'does not exist'. This is a pragmatic string-match approach consistent with the RepositoryManager error-message patterns already used throughout the codebase.

The _repoManager parameter is accepted by registerProjectRoutes() for API symmetry (WP spec requires it) but is not used directly — the ProjectManager internally calls repositoryManager.exists() via its own injected dependency. This matches the layered architecture already established.

comments.note: The _repoManager parameter is accepted by registerProjectRoutes() for API symmetry but is never called directly by route handlers — projectManager.addRepository() internally validates repo existence. MockRepositoryManager in test file only provides exists(), which is never invoked. This is correct architecture.

rename() and addRepository() error classification uses msg.includes('does not exist') to decide 404 vs 400. This is pragmatic and works correctly for all error messages in both MockProjectManager and real ProjectManager, but creates a soft coupling to error message wording.

flushAsync() helper (two process.nextTick calls) is a clean shared utility within the test file, avoiding repetitive await patterns. Consistent with the repositories.test.ts inline approach but more readable.

summary: Code review PASS for WP-006 (Project API Routes).

src/server/routes/projects.ts: Implements all 8 routes cleanly. Follows the same structural pattern as repositories.ts — isPlainObject() guard, parseJsonBody() for async handlers, sendJson/sendError wiring. No extraneous logic.

Error-classification pattern (lines 211, 270): `msg.includes('does not exist')` heuristic to discriminate 404 vs 400 is pragmatic and works correctly for all error paths in both the real ProjectManager and MockProjectManager. The soft coupling to error message wording is a known trade-off noted by both Developer and QA — it is acceptable here because: (1) the error messages are controlled within this codebase, (2) a typed error hierarchy would be a larger refactor out of scope for this WP. A comment on both call sites documents the rationale — good.

PUT /api/projects/:id correctly accepts partial updates (either Name or Description, or both). The `Object.keys(changes).length === 0` guard prevents no-op 200 responses. This is subtler logic than the other handlers and is correctly tested.

_repoManager parameter: accepted for API symmetry, never consumed directly by the route handlers (projectManager.addRepository() validates repo existence via its own injected RepositoryManager internally). This is the correct layered-architecture choice. The underscore prefix (`_repoManager`) signals the unused parameter clearly.

Test file: flushAsync() helper removes repetitive inline tick-awaiting, cleaner than inline pattern in repositories.test.ts. MockProjectManager is complete (7 methods + seed). seed() deep-copies Repositories arrays to prevent inter-test mutation. MockRepositoryManager is deliberately minimal (only seedIds/exists) because routes never call it directly. buildSut() with destructured { router, pm, rm } is idiomatic.
All 23 tests map cleanly to the 8 route handlers and all documented AC branches. 495/495 tests pass. All 6 ACs confirmed met.

comments.note: projects.ts defines isPlainObject() locally, identical to the copy in repositories.ts. Same duplication flagged in WP-005 review. As the route count grows, extracting this to requestUtils.ts would eliminate the pattern; currently low priority with only two files affected.

The string-match heuristic `msg.includes('does not exist')` for 404 vs 400 discrimination (lines 211 and 270) is documented in inline comments, which is good. A longer-term improvement would be a custom error type (e.g., NotFoundError extends Error) that the managers throw for ID-not-found cases, eliminating the wording dependency entirely. Out of scope for this WP.

DELETE /api/projects/:id/repositories/:repoId always returns 404 on any error from removeRepository() (line 286–288). removeRepository() only throws for 'project not found' or 'repo not linked' — both are semantically 404, so the blanket 404 mapping is correct here. Contrast with rename/addRepository which must distinguish 404 vs 400.

notes: All 6 ACs met. 495/495 tests pass. 8 route handlers fully covered. No regressions. Clean for code review.
